author: Chain_Affinity
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI - Disappointing After 13 Years

After 13 years of waiting, GTA 6 falls short of expectations. Despite impressive graphics, the game comes with plenty of frustrating decisions: a 30 FPS cap, bugs and crashes, tedious everyday chores, forced relationship mechanics, restricted player freedom, and a storyline that puts too much emphasis on Jason and Lucia's domestic relationship rather than the traditional GTA experience.

The gameplay reportedly feels slower, less edgy, and less unrestricted than previous entries. For a game with this much hype, development time, and money behind it, these shortcomings are difficult to overlook.

Overall: A massive missed opportunity. Impressive visuals don't compensate for questionable gameplay decisions and the departure from what made GTA great in the first place.

author: Chain_Affinity
quote:
A huge disappointment from Insomniac.

Marvel's Wolverine should have been an easy home run. Wolverine is one of Marvel's most iconic characters, and Insomniac has already demonstrated that it can create excellent superhero games. Unfortunately, the final product feels like a repetitive, heavily scripted cinematic action game that rarely delivers the freedom, brutality, or gameplay depth that a Wolverine game should have.

One of the biggest problems is the combat. It looks fine, but looks aren't enough. The actual fighting quickly becomes repetitive, with many encounters devolving into repeatedly attacking enemies with large health bars, performing the same finishers, and moving on to the next arena. Wolverine's claws should make combat feel vicious and distinctive, but the underlying mechanics often feel like a conventional action game with Wolverine's animations layered over them.

The progression system doesn't help. The skill tree is relatively shallow, and some of the more interesting abilities arrive too late to meaningfully change the experience. Instead of continually making Wolverine more exciting to control, progression often feels like unlocking things the character should have been capable of doing much earlier.

Exploration is another major disappointment. The game is extremely linear and constantly tells you where to go and what to do. The scent trail is particularly unnecessary. Rather than encouraging players to examine their surroundings and figure things out, the game frequently provides an obvious path directly to the objective. Collectibles and interactive objects are similarly difficult to miss. There is very little sense of discovery.

There is also far too much forced walking, scripted interaction, and cinematic interruption. You are given control of Wolverine, only to repeatedly have that control taken away so the game can perform another animation or deliver another conversation. Even some action sequences feel heavily automated. This makes the experience feel less like playing Wolverine and more like occasionally participating in a Wolverine movie.

The pacing suffers as a result. The game repeatedly alternates between spectacular cinematic sequences, slow walking sections, exposition, and familiar combat encounters. The individual set pieces can look incredible, but the gameplay connecting them together isn't nearly as impressive.

The story and characterization are also inconsistent. Wolverine should be one of the easiest Marvel characters to establish: violent, cynical, stubborn, dangerous, sarcastic and emotionally damaged, while still possessing a strong moral core. Instead, Logan sometimes feels noticeably softer and more agreeable than expected. The game also makes some questionable choices with established characters and relationships, while several potentially interesting characters don't receive the development they deserve.

The biggest issue is that the game doesn't consistently make you feel like Wolverine. That's the fundamental failure . A Wolverine game should make you feel like an almost unstoppable mutant who can charge directly into situations that would kill an ordinary person. His healing factor, claws, strength and aggression should fundamentally define the gameplay. Instead, Marvel's Wolverine frequently feels like a fairly conventional linear action game where the protagonist happens to be Wolverine.

The presentation is fine. The graphics are fine, except fluid (water, lava) animation. The animations are detailed. The voice acting is typical PlayStation mid. The violence and gore are appropriate for the character. The technical quality is considerably better than many poorly optimized AAA releases.

But, none of that fixes mediocre gameplay. This is particularly disappointing coming from Insomniac. The Spider-Man games demonstrated how to make simply moving around the world enjoyable. Wolverine doesn't have an equivalent gameplay-defining mechanic. Traversal frequently becomes something to get through rather than something to enjoy. The result is a game that looks like an enormous AAA production while often playing like a much smaller, more conventional action title. There are good moments here, but unfortunately, the good moments are surrounded by too much repetition, too much hand-holding, too much forced cinematic content, and too little meaningful player freedom.

Wolverine deserved a game built around what makes Wolverine unique. Instead, we got a polished cinematic action game that repeatedly gets in its own way.

And on top of all of that, it's a buggy mess, with technical problems that make an already disappointing experience even worse.

0/10 not because the graphics are bad. Not because the game is technically broken. Not because there is absolutely nothing good about it. 0/10 because the core experience fails to deliver the kind of Wolverine game it should have been.

Wolverine deserved better.

quote: I don’t know what I was expecting, but it certainly wasn’t this. It might have been the $90 price tag (I'm in Canada) that had me thinking I was getting a AAA next-gen experience, but I was very wrong. The graphics are improved, but the gameplay stinks of a two generation old 3D game. Even if you’ve never played this game before, the gameplay is so old and outdated. I’m giving it a 0 because this game is everything that is wrong with the industry. PlayStation is driven by corporate greed and charging people $70 - $100 for an old rehashed product in the middle of a recession is out of touch and just gross.
game_title: The Last of Us Part I

author: Chain_Affinity
quote:
This game should be called Bloodstained: Farming of the Night, because you'll be farming well into the night. Or Bloodstained: Ritual of the Farming, because it'll become a ritual every time you play. There's so much farming in this game, it's practically a farming simulator. I've never farmed so much in a game, and I've played some pretty intense MMO's throughout the years. You get the point.

Bloodstained should be a good game. It has all the elements to make a pretty engaging Metroidvania styled game. Here's the problem if you would like to get the most out of the game: It's 1% story, 6% actual gameplay, 15% exploration, and 78% farming.

author: Chain_Affinity
quote: I feel strongly attached to Death Stranding after playing it, as I thought it was an original, unique and incredible experience. But honestly, there's a whole category of gamers who probably didn't feel that way. Even on the highest difficulty setting, the shooting/fighting element of the game is trivially easy and a lot of people will see that as the main gameplay. I looked forward to the peaceful emptiness of the world on a long delivery run, but to others it feels desolate. I found it extremely gratifying in building structures to traverse the landscape while connecting people in need. Gameplay mechanics were interesting, fun and felt rewarding when you finished a run. I thoroughly enjoyed the story and felt it completely captivated me. A lot of people just won't enjoy the concept. I don't think that makes it any less of a masterpiece.

author: Chain_Affinity
quote: Lost Odyssey (in my opinion) is by far the best RPG exclusive to hit the Xbox 360 console. And any console for that matter. I have been a major fan of RPGs since the original Dragon Warrior hit the NES, and have since played all in that series along with many others, including the entire Final Fantasy franchise. Lost Odyssey definitely holds its own against any other title I've played, and in some ways surpasses the others. It has a deep and rich story, supported by memorable characters you easily get attached to and empathize with. The battle system and pacing of the game compliment each other perfectly. Art design and graphics are absolute eye candy, with an amazingly beautiful soundtrack and score, rivaling the music in many Final Fantasy titles. It isn't a surprise as it is composed by the legend Nobuo Uematsu himself. With Xbox One backwards compatibility, I feel fans of RPGs owe it to themselves to experience this title at least once.
